newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says stolen art withdrawn from auction.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says stolen art withdrawn from auction.

text.p: Two Indonesian artworks were withdrawn from a sale by international auction house Christies last week after it was revealed they had been stolen from Jakarta's National Museum, media reports said on Tuesday.
The Jakarta Post newspaper quoted Education and Culture Minister Wardiman Djojonegoro as saying the theft took place a month ago and was believed to have involved members of the museum's staff.
"The stolen paintings have been withdrawn by Christies," Djojonegoro said.

The theft was revealed after Christies published a catalogue for its October 6 sale, in Singapore, containing two paintings -- "A Nude", completed in 1992 by Basoeki Abdullah, and "Potrait of a Dutch Governor Wearing the Willems Order", painted in 1867 by Raden Saleh.
The auctioneers withdrew the two paintings on Friday.
The newspaper said altoghether six paintings, by Raden Saleh, Basoeki Abdullah and Affandi, had been stolen from the museum and the theft was reported to police on September 12.
Djojonegoro said the theft might have been motivated by the low wages of museum employees. Middle-ranked Indonesian civil servants earn between 250,000 rupiah ($108) and 500,000 ($216) a month.
